text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — proposing an 'edge cache' shim for private controlplane handoffs. idea is to keep a tiny, region-local relay that caches auth tokens + certs for tenants to reduce handshake traffic and preserve egress IP affinity when we fall back from privatelink -> relay.
ajay: short + curious — how is this different from our existing relay? sounds like an extra moving part.
devon: gist: current relay is heavyweight (full proxy), this would be a minimal stateful cache (TTL'd tokens, KV for certs) that only answers handshake/proof-of-possession and routes to controlplane. small memory footprint, sticky to AZ.
sophia: biggest questions: (1) security/attack surface for cached certs, (2) rotation semantics, (3) ops surface (alerts/cleanup)
maria: agreed. plan: HSM/KMS-wrapped keys only, ephemeral cache entries bound to tenant + nonce, automatic eviction on revocation. doesn't hold long-term material. ACLs + mTLS for controlplane connections.
ajay: concern: egress IP preservation — if cache is regional then traffic still SNATs via relay. we need to ensure we can map back to original tenant IPs for third-party allowlists.
devon: propose outgoing path: tenant -> privatelink (preferred) else -> edge-cache (ENI in customer VPC or shared regional ENI?) we discussed both. edge-cache would source-NAT to a per-tenant egress pool we manage so we can preserve stable IPs per customer tier.
sophia: per-tenant egress pool has capacity and cost implications. also IPv6? many customers want dualstack. do we maintain pools for both families?
maria: start with IPv4 only for MVP; document IPv6 followup. cost: can gate on committed capacity for Dedicated/Private customers — self-service request for reserved IPs.
infra-bot: deploy-check: rolling canary required for any edge-cache image that touches keys. Please schedule canary in us-west-2 only.
ajay: rollout Q — do we need to change onboarding for new Private customers? currently we issue controlplane creds and set up privatelink. with cache, we need to provision cache ACL + optional egress IP lease.
devon: onboarding delta: add optional field in registry -> "egress_mode": [privatelink, cache-egress, shared-egress], and a lease ticket flow for cache. implementation: API change + migration script for existing customers (default keep as today).
sophia: testing matrix: 1) privatelink happy path, 2) failover to cache (handshake + cert fetch), 3) concurrent cert rotation, 4) IP lease exhaustion, 5) eviction under revocation.
maria: security note: cache must log token access but obfuscate token values in logs. also require attestation that cache instances run verified images (sigstore or similar).
ajay: operational visibility: add metrics: handshake_latency, cache_hit_rate, per-tenant_egress_ip_used_count, lease_free_count. Alert: >1% handshake errors over 5m.
devon: timeline sketch: week 0-2 spike/proof-of-concept + threat model, week 3-5 implement cache RPC + registry API, week 6 canary in us-west-2, week 7 expand regionally, week 8 migrate opt-in customers and collect SLOs.
sophia: fallback semantics: if cache can't reach controlplane, should we fail open or hard fail? leaning hard fail for controlplane operations that create creds, but for token refresh maybe return 503 to client so app retries.
maria: agree. conservative: don't create new tokens if controlplane unreachable; allow read-only operations from cache if previously permitted.
ajay: edge case: what if privatelink exists but DNS resolves differently and we accidentally double-route? need clear precedence: privatelink > direct private endpoint > edge-cache.
devon: add a small code snippet for precedence in agent config:

```
# agent egress precedence
egress_order:
  - privatelink
  - private_endpoint
  - edge_cache
  - internet_fallback
```
sophia: ops checklist before canary: IAM roles, KMS keys ready, sigstore validation, metrics+dashboards, canary rollback playbook.
maria: ok I'll open a follow-up RFC doc for the design details + threat model. for this thread: ask for thumbs and any blockers.
ajay: :thumbsup: 1 blocker — need cost estimate for per-tenant IP pools. can someone pair with finance?
sophia: I'll take that with finance, pinging @finance in the doc.
devon: minor: we should consider coalescing revocation events into a single sweep to avoid thundering herd on cache.
infra-bot: note: created ticket INFRA-3491 for canary checklist.
maria: thanks — I'll update RFC and add migration script notes. closing thread for now unless new blockers crop up.
